notes: Pure UI cycle per RULINGS.md Process section: no loremaster/tutorial gate. Demo target: ui-demos/inbox-v3/index.html. Position taken on the two-focal-candidate question: LIST's focal is the DAY numeral (nothing else on that sparse screen earns extreme scale); CARD's focal is DOMINANT ROUTINE + THREAT TIER, per the brief's argument (this is a decision surface: what am I walking into). Position taken on the two-state problem: WIDTH survives as a single steps() transition (LIST is genuinely narrower, no second column to arrange), and the 700/820px height claim is judged on the CARD/OPEN state, which is the taller of the two by design; LIST is deliberately NOT padded to match CARD's height; a shorter idle-state window is a bigger tiling win, not a smaller one. Also folded in one correction: shipped inbox.tsx flags STRAIN crimson when `strain > 70`, which is backwards against the mechanic (strain severs at zero, so low strain is the risk band, matching loadout-eva's ruling). This surface fixes the polarity but does NOT give STRAIN --r-warn: the brief reserves that role for the head-start WARNING alone (RULINGS law 1, 'exactly one thing per surface'), so STRAIN reads as plain ambient data here; a strain alarm belongs on REPAIR.LOG per the panel queue.

items.spec: INBOX + CUSTOMER.REC rebuilt as a KP/OS v3 instrument panel. Reference: ui-demos/loadout-eva/index.html. Copy verbatim: the :root role-token block and the two data-scheme blocks (nerv/tokyo, lines 44-141 of that file), the six .lo-glass CRT layers and FLAT/OFF wiring (lines 264-330), the .lo-fit/.lo-stage true-resolution-then-transform-scale rig, the countUp/typeIn/later helpers, the difference-blend risk-flash technique (.lo-riskflash, lo-risk-blink keyframe), and the kp-slot-in / kp-page-flip / kp-fw-in keyframes from _shared/kp.css and system.css. Prefix all new classes `ib-`. === GLANCE ORDER === LIST state (run.screen==='day', no job open): 1st DAY hero numeral (masthead). 2nd the three ticket rows (each row's own tier-pips+pay is a small internal hierarchy). Ambient: footer chips (STRAIN/CR/RAM/POUCH/KIT), hint line. CARD state (run.screen==='analyze', job open): 1st DOMINANT ROUTINE label + THREAT TIER pip row, paired as one focal cluster at extreme scale (this is the decision: what am I walking into). 2nd the verdict/action band: DIVE + TICKET RATE + YOUR KIT chip + CONFIGURE KIT/BACK. 3rd support band: NAME/DEVICE with portrait+device cells, GRID/RAM ticks, WARNING (day 3+ only). Ambient: the list column (now secondary, ticket rows still switchable), footer chips. DAY numeral is NOT hero-scale once a card is open (it demotes to a small masthead chip); this is a deliberate handoff, not a shrink-everything move. Type scale, all clamp() on cqi, VT323/Silkscreen floors held (19-21px body, 9-11px label), on a nested container structure: `.ib-eva{container-type:inline-size;container-name:ib}` wraps the whole window body (drives the 700px WIDE/NARROW breakpoint for the CARD state's two-column arrangement only); `.ib-card-pane{container-type:inline-size;container-name:card}` wraps just the open card pane (drives the DOMINANT hero's own scale against its actual column width, cqi-in-custom-property resolves at use site per the loadout precedent). --ib-fs-body: clamp(19px, calc(1cqi + 17px), 21px) [loadout's body ramp, reused verbatim] --ib-fs-label: clamp(9px, calc(0.6cqi + 8px), 11px) [loadout's label ramp, reused verbatim] --ib-fs-tickl: clamp(8px, calc(0.4cqi + 7.5px), 9px); --ib-fs-tickv: clamp(12px, calc(0.8cqi + 10px), 14px) [loadout's tick ramps] --ib-fs-day (LIST focal, against `ib` container): clamp(40px, 14cqi, 88px). At LIST-only content width ~422px this lands ~59px vs body 21px = 2.8x contrast. --ib-fs-day-chip (masthead DAY when a card is open, demoted): fixed, reuse .kp-chip-pct value size (13px), not fluid. --ib-fs-dominant (CARD focal, against `card` container): clamp(48px, 16cqi, 92px). At laptop card-pane width ~470px lands ~75px (3.6x body); at 16:9 ~550px lands ~88px; at 21:9 ~610px clamps to the 92px ceiling. Always comfortably above the 2.2x law-2 minimum at every supported viewport. THREAT TIER pips: fixed-size .kp-pip-diamond (17px), not fluid; they are the focal cluster's second channel, not typography, so they don't need a ramp. === ZONES / GRID === One window, two DOM shapes gated by whether a job is open (mirrors inbox.tsx's `open` state machine, structure unchanged). LIST-only markup: zones mast, list, foot only; layout is ALWAYS a single column at a fixed compact width (460px window at every supported viewport) and is not subject to the 700px breakpoint below (it has no second column to arrange, so it never falls into the narrow stack fallback; that fallback exists only for extreme tiling of the CARD/open state). CARD-open markup adds zones focal, verdict, support inside a second column. WIDE tier (content inline-size >= 700px on the `ib` container; this is the CARD state's own breakpoint): ``` grid-template-columns: 340px 1fr; grid-template-areas: "mast mast" "list focal" "list verdict" "list support" "foot foot"; ``` list spans all three middle rows beside focal/verdict/support (law 8's 'a row you do not share is a row you pay for in full': the list column is shorter than the stacked focal+verdict+support column, so sharing those rows is free, exactly the loadout gutter-beside-trinity technique). @container ib (min-width: 700px) is the exact breakpoint (matches the system standard). At the three supported viewports the CARD-open content inline-size is approx 902px (16:9, window 940), 962px (21:9, window 1000), 822px (laptop, window 860): all comfortably above 700, so all three render WIDE, per law 3. NARROW fallback (@container ib (max-width: 699.98px), CARD state only, tiling fallback, no supported viewport reaches it): single column, areas stack `mast` `list` `focal` `verdict` `support` `foot` in order; ticket rows compact (pips only, subject truncates harder); no tab strip needed since content is now light enough to simply stack (unlike loadout's trinity, there is no third axis of content competing for the same space here). Container widths: LIST-only window 460px at every viewport (constant; a list has no reason to grow with the desk). CARD-open window: 940px (16:9), 1000px (21:9), 860px (laptop) (matches loadout's per-viewport scaling pattern). List column fixed 340px inside CARD state at every tier. === ROLE TOKENS === --r-struct: window border, masthead/card/row hairline borders, dividers. --r-note: all `// LABEL` prefixes and eyebrows ("INBOX // DAY LOOP", "// CUSTOMER.REC" eyebrow, "// DOMINANT ROUTINE" label above the hero, NAME/DEVICE field labels, GRID/RAM tick labels, YOUR KIT label). --r-line: THREAT TIER pip fills (both in ticket rows and the CARD focal cluster), GRID/RAM tick values, the footer strain-bar segments (ambient, no alarm behavior). --r-data: DOMINANT ROUTINE hero text (CARD focal, biggest text on that state), DAY hero numeral (LIST focal), TICKET RATE / pay chip values, STRAIN numeral (ambient hero within the footer chip only, not a surface-level focal). --r-ok: the CLEARED tag text on a done ticket row (a resolved/nominal verdict, not a live alarm) plus the corner-tick reticle marking the currently OPEN ticket (a second channel on top of its border highlight, matching loadout's mode-on reticle). --r-warn: EXACTLY the head-start WARNING row (day.headStart > 0 only), nothing else. Its second channel is REQUIRED and is two things at once: (a) the row floods inverse video (--r-warn fill, void text, the shipped danger idiom), and (b) a composited opacity difference-blend plate over the row blinks on the shipped 1.2s steps(2) cadence (.lo-riskflash technique verbatim, promoted layer, opacity-only, no repaint cost). THREAT TIER pips never take --r-warn at any tier, including on the DAY 7 late state where a WARNING is also live: the two must read as visually distinct systems (tier = --r-line diamonds; risk = --r-warn flooded row that moves). STRAIN, even when numerically low, stays plain (--r-data numeral, --r-line bar fill): this surface's one alarm is the head-start WARNING per the brief, and RULINGS law 1 caps a surface at exactly one --r-warn user. --r-aux: the portrait/device 1-bit image cells' ink-tint multiply overlay (a different signal class from bench data, per law 5/loadout precedent). --r-hazard: the window's 3px border, and ONE hazard-stripe divider (45deg repeating-linear-gradient) between the `list` column top and the `focal` zone, labeled "// DOSSIER" (--r-note text on the divider label itself, hazard only on the stripe fill). === CUTS (LAW 8, IN ORDER) === 1. Decorative imagery that cannot survive its size, cut outright: the PrintMark (81-cell dither fingerprint block), the eye-crop (second cropped detail of the portrait, redundant with the portrait cell itself), the CardScope oscilloscope trace, and the 12-row HexRows table. All four were pure techno-flavor with no decision-relevant data; none could shrink into the new footprint without dissolving into noise. 2. The CUSTOMER.REC boxed header + its 4-bar battery glyph icon: the battery glyph is decorative (no data) and is cut; the header text itself is not cut but demoted from a heavy boxed panel-head to a small `// CUSTOMER.REC` eyebrow line above the focal hero, folding its identity role into the masthead rather than paying for a second header band. 3. The INTAKE quote (customer's own words) moves from an always-visible block to a tap/hover/focus popup anchored on the NAME row, which carries a persistent dotted underline (the tier-0 'this holds more' marker, loadout precedent) so the affordance is discoverable at rest, not a dead end. Rationale: it is voice/flavor, not decision-critical, unlike the READOUT tell which stays always-visible because it is the tactical hint the glance order exists to serve. 4. GRID and INTRUSION RAM drop their boxed kp-datarow treatment and become unboxed ticks (label above value, no border), matching loadout's .lo-tick pattern: they are bench-diagnostic specs, lower priority than DOMINANT/TIER/WARNING/NAME/DEVICE, and the data itself is kept, only the box is cut. 5. Paging/tabs reserved for the NARROW fallback only (see ZONES); not needed at any supported viewport since the WIDE tier already fits under the ceiling once 1-4 are applied. Kept without modification, because the brief explicitly asks for them specified rather than cut: the two 1-bit portrait/device cells (resized as a crop, see IMAGERY), the WARNING row, the READOUT tell, THREAT TIERS (promoted into the focal cluster, not cut), TICKET RATE (moved into the verdict zone). === IMAGERY === All portrait/device cells render their source PNG at 1:1 (image-rendering:pixelated, no CSS width/height scaling on the itself), inside an `overflow:hidden` cell exactly the crop's target size; the crop is a CSS `position:absolute; top:-Npx; left:-Mpx` offset on the , never a resample, per loadout's .lo-mon technique. Cell size: 128x128 CSS px for both portrait and device, side by side (8px gap) in the support zone. Ink-tint (--r-aux multiply overlay) is the default treatment; see IMAGE TREATMENT variation for TRUE 1-BIT / FULL COLOUR. Crop boxes (native source is 304x304 unless noted; offsets are the position, i.e. how far the native image is shifted up/left inside the 128x128 window): - juno-vex portrait (304x304): offset top -38px, left -68px (centers the face/eyes). - juno-vex device (304x304, Hexlight handheld): offset top -50px, left -20px (frames the grip/button cluster, avoiding the blown-out screen). - aldous-wick portrait (304x304): offset top -86px, left -76px (centers the face). - aldous-wick device (304x304, Meridian ledger terminal): offset top -26px, left -146px (frames the CRT screen). - wren-tallis device (304x304, mixer console): offset top -66px, left -76px (frames the VU-meter dial cluster). Fallback for a customer with no portrait print (wren-tallis, and any future roster gap): a 128x128 1-bit dithered NO-SIGNAL plate (checker/static dither at the same treatment tint as a live cell, --r-struct border identical to a filled cell) captioned "NO PRINT ON FILE" in --r-note at --ib-fs-tickl, same footprint as a filled cell so the two-cell row never reflows depending on roster coverage. Diegetic framing: the file simply has no photo on record yet. === RUN STATES (exact data, do not invent beyond this) === State A, "DAY 1 OPENER" (sparse): day 1, runNumber 1, FINAL_DAY 10, credits 0, strain 100, ramPerTurn 5, patchPouch [] (0/5), kit scanTier1/attackTier1/defendTier1, attackMode redirect, defendMode purge, augments []. Jobs: [0] juno-vex tier1 dominant armSiphon quoteIndex0 (OPEN for the CARD demo; jobPay(1)=65cr); [1] sable-okonkwo tier1 dominant redirect quoteIndex0; [2] aldous-wick tier1 dominant armHalt quoteIndex0. jobsDone [false,false,false]. State B, "DAY 4 FULL SLATE" (default state): day 4, runNumber 7, credits 185, strain 78, ramPerTurn 6, patchPouch 3 pieces (masks 0x5, 0x3, 0xf; 3/5), kit scanTier2/attackTier1/defendTier2, attackMode redirect, defendMode purge, augments 2 (HOT BOOT, CLEAN RUN, for the KIT chip only, not rendered as cards on this surface). Day config (DAY_CONFIGS[4]): grid [9,9], oppRam 6, headStart 2 (WARNING: "Intrusion already 2 nodes deep"). jobTiers [2,2,3]. Jobs: [0] wren-tallis tier2 dominant ward quoteIndex1 (OPEN for the CARD demo, exercises the no-portrait fallback live; jobPay(2)=90cr); [1] sable-okonkwo tier2 dominant redirect quoteIndex0; [2] dex-marlowe tier3 dominant redirect quoteIndex0. jobsDone [false,false,false]. State C, "DAY 7 LATE" (warning + cleared): day 7, runNumber 7, credits 340, strain 52, ramPerTurn 7, patchPouch 2 pieces (masks 0x3, 0x7; 2/5), kit scanTier3/attackTier2/defendTier2, attackMode armSiphon, defendMode ward, augments 4. Day config (DAY_CONFIGS[7]): grid [11,11], oppRam 7, headStart 3 (WARNING: "Intrusion already 3 nodes deep"). jobTiers [3,3,4]. Jobs: [0] bram-hollander tier3 dominant lock quoteIndex1, jobsDone[0]=true (CLEARED, struck through, disabled, equal-footprint row); [1] aldous-wick tier3 dominant armHalt quoteIndex1 (OPEN for the CARD demo; jobPay(3)=115cr); [2] ines-calloway tier4 dominant armHalt quoteIndex0. jobsDone [true,false,false]. All customer/tier pairs verified against customers.ts `tiers` arrays and arc.ts DAY_CONFIGS jobTiers. Subject lines: use the shipped SUBJECTS record verbatim for every customer named above (all 6 already have routed lines). === LOAD CHOREOGRAPHY (mount / REPLAY LOAD, resets to LIST-only) === All steps(), all timers via later()/setTimeout (never rAF, so an occluded window doesn't stall mid-sequence), instant under prefers-reduced-motion. t=0: masthead chrome (border, eyebrow, INBOX label) present instantly, no animation (ambient chrome per law 7 never animates). t=0-180ms: DAY hero numeral counts up 0 -> target (countUp, 30ms interval, ~6 steps for single/double-digit days). t=150ms, staggered 90ms apart: each ticket row slides in (kp-slot-in, 300ms steps(5)), its tier-pip row fills 40ms after its own row lands, its pay/CLEARED value types or counts in. t=150+2*90+300=630ms: footer chips slot in: STRAIN counts up (30ms interval) at t=650, CR at t=690, RAM at t=730, POUCH glyphs stagger 80ms apart starting t=770 (skipped entirely, 0ms, if patchPouch is empty), KIT chip types at t=850. Settle ~1.3s total (shorter than loadout's ~2.4s: this surface carries less content). === OPEN / CLOSE (LIST <-> CARD), single steps() transition per axis === Open (click an undone ticket): (1) sfx inboxGrow, height axis: measure the destination CARD height off a hidden instant-render clone (mirrors inbox.tsx's existing measure/paneWidth technique verbatim), commit start height, step to target over 200ms steps(5) via direct style writes (a one-shot handful of reflows, not a continuous animation, so this is fine even though height is a layout property: the CRT no longer runs a displacement filter over the stage in FLAT/OFF, so there is no repaint-triggers-refilter cost left to avoid here; that concern is specifically about the ALARM's continuous loop, which is compositor-only per below). (2) at +200ms, sfx inboxWide, width axis: the card-pane wrapper steps from width:0/opacity:0 to its measured target width/opacity:1 over 200ms steps(4) (ib-pane-in keyframe, mirrors loadout's kp-fw-in cadence). (3) at +400ms, sfx inboxGenie, the card content genies out of the clicked row's vertical center (transform-origin set via JS to that row's midpoint, exactly the shipped paneRef technique), scaleY 0.2->1 + opacity, 210ms steps(6). (4) IF day.headStart > 0: layer the new ibWarnReveal one-shot under the genie sfx at the same +400ms mark, so a late-run card announces its own weight distinctly from an early one. Total open ~610ms. Close (click the open ticket again, or BACK): reverse order and roughly reverse timing: sfx inboxFile + card shrinks into its row (180ms), width narrows (200ms), height settles (240ms). Total ~620ms. This whole sequence is the shipped choreography's structure, re-measured against the new (much lighter) content rather than dropped, per the brief's explicit direction. All of the above are ONE-SHOT discrete transitions, not loops; the only continuous/looping animation on this surface is the WARNING row's risk-flash, which is the one built compositor-only (opacity on a promoted layer, will-change:opacity), per RULINGS law 7's measured example. === BUILD NOTES === Standalone page, vanilla JS, no framework, per RULINGS recipe: `ui-demos/inbox-v3/index.html` linking `../_shared/kp.css` + `../_shared/system.css`, art under `ui-demos/inbox-v3/art/` (copies of the shipped card-*-portrait/device PNGs; no new generation, art budget is NONE per the brief). Register in ui-demos/manifest.json at status:awaiting with variation rows SCHEME/CRT/VIEWPORT/RUN STATE/WINDOW STATE/IMAGE TREATMENT.
acceptance: DOMINANT ROUTINE text is measurably the single largest text on the CARD state (>=2.2x the 19-21px body floor) at every viewport; DAY numeral is measurably the single largest text on the LIST state.

grep the built stylesheet: `--r-warn` is applied to exactly one selector on this page (the WARNING row), and that selector also carries a steps(2) opacity keyframe (its second channel) plus an inverse-video fill; no THREAT TIER pip selector anywhere (LIST rows or CARD focal) ever resolves --r-warn, checked specifically on the DAY 7 state where a WARNING is simultaneously live.
STRAIN chip never takes --r-warn or any alarm treatment in any state, including at strain 52 (State C); it reads as plain data.
no internal scrollbar in LIST or CARD state at any of the 3 viewports; no border-radius on any UI chrome element (glass/bezel excluded); no em or en dash anywhere on the page.
both NERV and TOKYO NIGHT schemes resolve all eight roles to visibly distinct colors on this panel (screenshot diff or computed-style check per role).

all three supported viewports (1366x768, 2560x1080, 1280x800 laptop) render the CARD state's WIDE two-column arrangement (no narrow-tier stack triggers); LIST-only state renders its single fixed-width column at all three.
measured LIST-only content height <= 500px at all 3 viewports (well under the 700px target).

measured CARD-open content height <= 700px target (hard fail above 820px) at all 3 viewports, measured on State C (DAY 7 LATE), the tallest run state (WARNING row + CLEARED row + fullest pouch/kit chips).

both portrait and device elements render at native pixel scale in every state (naturalWidth/naturalHeight equal to rendered width/height; only the parent cell's overflow:hidden crops what is visible), at every viewport.
the no-print fallback (wren-tallis in State B) renders at the identical 128x128 footprint as a filled cell, with no layout shift versus a filled row.
switching between all 3 run states and both window states never leaves more than one ticket row's typewriter/count-up running at a time (per-row token scoping, mirroring loadout's per-panel scoping).
clicking a CLEARED/done ticket is a no-op; its row occupies the identical height as an active row (equal-footprint law).
prefers-reduced-motion collapses the load sweep, the open/close choreography, and the WARNING risk-flash to their settled end state in a single frame; sound is unaffected.
the open/close choreography's height-axis step never exceeds 5 discrete frames (steps(5)) and produces no visible tear between the height, width, and genie phases when scrubbed frame by frame.

items.when: layered under inboxGenie at the CARD open choreography's genie phase, only when the opened job's day.headStart > 0 (day 3+): a low tense one-shot marking that this ticket's intrusion is already partway in, distinct from an early-run card's plain genie.
